rulings.restated: Choose — [helper "Positive foreign taxes" = true → helper "Smaller of ftc.taxes, f1040.line16"] [helper "Positive foreign taxes" = false → helper "Year parameter sales.zero"]
rulings.model: The branching and the refusal are right. However, when foreign tax is positive the credit takes the 'limited' value, which measures regular tax as Form 1040 line 16 alone instead of 'the total of Form 1040... line 16, and Schedule 2 (Form 1040), Part I, line 1z, less any tax included on line 16 from Form 4972'. So the credit can differ from 'the smaller of (a) your total foreign tax, or (b) your regular tax.'
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope/representation on supported completed individual returns; i1116 (2025) pp.1–2 requires the smaller of foreign tax and regular tax, with p.25 Line20 defining regular tax as Form1040 line16 plus Schedule2 PartI line1z less Form4972 tax, with Form8978 adjustments. s2.other explicitly excludes advance-credit repayments and every other unsupported Schedule2 tax and is enforced at s2.line3/line21. scope.other_line16 excludes Forms4972/8978 and is enforced at f1040.line16. Thus the additional terms are zero on supported completed returns; Form1040 line16 is the regular-tax amount in this slice. Stand-alone excluded cases are not claimed equivalent. The reviewer correctly identifies the full IRS rule; its reduction here depends on those declared refusals, not model noise.

rulings.restated: Choose — [helper "Positive foreign taxes" = true → helper "Smaller of ftc.taxes, f1040.line16"] [helper "Positive foreign taxes" = false → helper "Year parameter sales.zero"]
rulings.model: The structure (smaller of foreign tax or regular tax, zero if no foreign tax, refusal to Form 1116 when the election fails) is consistent with the text. However, it depends on the 'limited' operand, whose definition of regular tax is in line 20 instructions that are not provided.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. Regular tax for the election is "your total U.S. income tax against which the credit is allowed (regular tax liability, as defined in section 26(b)(1))", excluding the net investment income tax (i1116 p. 25, line 20), which on the return in this slice is Form 1040 line 16: the additional line-16 taxes are refused by `scope.other_line16` and the net investment income and additional Medicare taxes sit on Schedule 2, after line 16. No change to the data.

rulings.model: The text says to enter 'the smaller of (a) your total foreign tax, or (b) your regular tax' and to 'See the instructions for line 20... for how to figure your regular tax'. For individuals, line 20 means 'the total of Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 16, and Schedule 2 (Form 1040), Part I, line 1z, less any tax included on line 16 from Form 4972' (adjusted for Form 8978). The program uses Form 1040 line 16 alone: it leaves out Schedule 2 line 1z and does not subtract the Form 4972 tax.
